attribution.note: Both occurrences are Marcus's own posts in his own voice. He rejects Musk's prediction and offers his own bet. Musk's words are quoted only as the target.

semantics.note: Offering a $1M bet that superhuman AGI 'would not arrive by the end of 2025' is an unhedged commitment, so it counts as a forecast. Saying he was 'skeptical' does not weaken it, because the bet fixes the outcome. The proposition keeps the end-2025 horizon and Marcus's own reading of the claim: AI that can do any intellectual work any human can do.

contract.note: The support test follows Marcus's own test: one piece of intellectual work top humans can do that AI cannot. One caveat: no single human solved all of ARC-AGI-2 either. But every task was solved by at least two people, and the best AI failed about 46% of them, so human-solvable tasks the AI failed exist under any reasonable reading.

evidence.note: ARC Prize Foundation results dated 5 Dec 2025, before the deadline. They give the best verified AI scores on ARC-AGI-2: 37.6% for a commercial model and 54% for a refinement system. No verified system solved the full set. This is the foundation's own measurement, not a statement by any AI lab.

ARC-AGI-2 paper from May 2025. It reports that every task was solved by at least two people in two attempts or less. Read with the December AI scores, it shows human-solvable reasoning tasks that no verified AI system solved by the end of 2025.

output.rationale: The horizon (end of 2025) has passed. Measurements dated before the deadline show the best verified AI systems solved at most 54% of ARC-AGI-2 tasks, and every task had been solved by at least two people. So intellectual work existed that humans could do and AI could not, which is Marcus's own test. The packet contains nothing suggesting any AI could do all human intellectual work by 2025-12-31. The forecast is supported.
